title: India Clinch Sepaktakraw Bronze After Narrow Semifinal Loss to Japan
excerpt: India's men's quadrant team went down 0-2 to Japan in the sepaktakraw semifinal at Nagoya, securing the country's third Asian Games medal in the sport and its first in the quadrant event.
body:
• India's men's quadrant team won bronze in sepaktakraw at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games, going down 0-2 to hosts Japan in the semifinal at Nagoya City Mizuho Park Gymnasium on October 2.
  • The semifinal was decided by narrow margins — 12-15, 13-15 — with Malemnganba Singh Sorokhaibam, Ram Kumar Sharma, Bobby Kumar and Akash Yumnam pushing the Japanese quartet in both sets.
  • This is only India's third sepaktakraw medal at the Asian Games, after the men's team regu bronze in 2018 and the women's team regu bronze in 2023 — and the country's first in the quadrant event.
  • The bronze caps an unbeaten group-stage run that included a stunning upset over World Cup winners Myanmar, plus wins over Vietnam and Laos.

India's men's quadrant secured a bronze medal in sepaktakraw at the Asian Games 2026 on Friday, losing to hosts Japan 0-2 in the semifinal at the Nagoya City Mizuho Park Gymnasium. The Indian quartet of Malemnganba Singh Sorokhaibam, Ram Kumar Sharma, Bobby Kumar and Akash Yumnam (with substitutes Lokhon Singh Elangbam and Tekong Arun) went down by close margins of 12-15, 13-15 to Japan's Yuki Sato, Ryota Haruhara, Wataru Narawa and Yota Ichikawa, according to IANS.

Context & Background

Sepaktakraw — the Southeast Asian sport played with a rattan ball struck over a net using feet, head and chest — has been an Asian Games staple, but India has rarely featured on its podium. This bronze is only India's third sepaktakraw medal in Asiad history: a men's team regu bronze at Jakarta 2018, followed by a women's team regu bronze at Hangzhou 2023. It is the country's first medal in the quadrant event.

The run to the podium was built on an upset. India topped Group A unbeaten, winning all three matches — stunning World Cup winners Myanmar in the league stage before beating Vietnam and Laos to reach the semifinals, which guaranteed the bronze. The medal was India's sixth on Friday, on a day that also saw Lovlina Borgohain win boxing gold and the women's recurve archery team stun 10-time champions South Korea for gold, according to IANS.

Not everything went India's way in sepaktakraw. The women's quadrant crashed out fourth in Group A with no wins, the women's doubles finished fourth in their group without a win, and the men's regu team failed to reach the knockouts after finishing third in Group B.

Impact & Analysis

The margins — two sets lost by a combined eight points — show how close India came to a first-ever final. Japan, backed by a home crowd, held their nerve in the closing rallies; India's group-stage form suggests the gap at Asia's top level is narrowing rather than static. The Myanmar upset in particular signals that this is a squad capable of beating the sport's traditional powers, not merely collecting a semifinal guarantee.

"The team fought hard. This is a significant achievement for Indian Sepaktakraw — the country's first-ever Asian Games medal in the Men's Quadrant event."

— Yogi Adityanath, UP Chief Minister, congratulating the team

The bronze also matters institutionally. Sepaktakraw's heartland in India is Manipur and the Northeast — the squad's names reflect that — and a first quadrant medal gives the federation a result to anchor funding and development conversations around, the way the 2018 and 2023 bronzes sustained the regu programmes.

Diaspora Angle

This is a medal with a specific regional resonance abroad. The Northeast Indian diaspora — communities in the UK, US, Canada and Australia — has long championed sepaktakraw as a sport where their states lead the nation; a national podium finish validates that pride on Asia's biggest stage. For diaspora sports followers tracking India's wider medal tally, the bronze adds depth to a contingent sitting at 72 medals.

What's Next

The team returns with a medal and a clear next target: converting semifinal appearances into finals at the next Asian cycle and the World Cup. For the federation, the task is sustaining the momentum in the men's programme while rebuilding the women's squads, which left Nagoya without a knockout appearance.
